proofs.proof_tex:
We construct the rational modulus first and then the point and interval evaluators.

\emph{Step 1: finite rational parameter bounds.}
Because the supplied name is nested, has widths tending to zero, and preserves the strict positivity conditions in Definition \(\mathrm{input\mbox{-}name}\), a finite prefix supplies rational numbers
\[
 0<\lambda_-\leq\lambda\leq\lambda_+,
 \quad 0<\tau_-\leq\tau\leq\tau_+,
 \quad 0<\nu_-\leq\nu\leq\nu_+,                              \tag{1}
\]
together with rational upper bounds \(c_M^+\geq c_M\), \(c_I^+\geq c_I\), a rational lower bound \(0<\alpha_-\leq\alpha\), and a rational upper bound for \(G\).  Define the positive rationals
\[
 \begin{gathered}
 d_-=\lambda_-+\tau_-,\qquad d_+=\lambda_++\tau_+,\qquad
 D_+=\lambda_++\tau_++\nu_+,\\
 q_-=\frac{\lambda_-(\tau_-+\nu_-)}{D_+},\qquad
 q_+=\frac{\lambda_+(\tau_++\nu_+)}{\lambda_-+\tau_-+\nu_-},
 \qquad
 v_*=\frac{2\lambda_-\tau_-}{d_+^3}.
                                                                    \tag{2}
 \end{gathered}
\]
The defining formulas for \(d,D,q,V_0\) and (1) imply
\[
 d_-\leq d\leq d_+,\qquad D\leq D_+,\qquad
 q_-\leq q\leq q_+,\qquad V_0\geq v_*>0.                       \tag{3}
\]
Rational bisection, certified by comparisons of squared rational endpoints, produces positive rationals \(s_q,s_d,s_0\) such that
\[
 s_q^2\geq q_+,\qquad s_d^2\leq d_-,\qquad s_0^2\leq v_*.      \tag{4}
\]
Lemma \(\mathrm{gamma\mbox{-}energy\mbox{-}lipschitz}\), (3), and (4) give the rational uniform bound
\[
 |V_\gamma'|
 \leq K_V:=\frac{5\nu_+s_q}{d_-^2s_d}.                        \tag{5}
\]

Enumerate positive integers \(H\) and certify, using the rational exponential enclosures constructed below, the strict inequality
\[
 \frac{e^{-H^2/2}}H<\frac{\alpha_-}{2}.                        \tag{6}
\]
This enumeration terminates because its left side tends to zero.  The elementary Gaussian tail calculation
\[
 1-\Phi(H)
 =\frac1{\sqrt{2\pi}}\int_H^\infty e^{-x^2/2}\,dx
 \leq\frac{e^{-H^2/2}}{H\sqrt{2\pi}}
 <\frac{\alpha_-}{2}                                           \tag{7}
\]
uses integration by parts and \(\sqrt{2\pi}>1\).  Since \(\alpha\geq\alpha_-\), (7) implies \(z_\alpha<H\).  Moreover, (3)--(4) show
\(\sqrt{V_0+V_\gamma}\geq\sqrt{V_0}\geq s_0\).  Differentiating the design objective and using (5) therefore yields
\[
 |\partial_\gamma J(p,\gamma)|
 \leq c_M^++\frac{c_I^+HK_V}{2s_0}.                            \tag{8}
\]
Thus the explicitly constructed positive integer
\[
 L_J=1+\left\lceil c_M^++\frac{c_I^+HK_V}{2s_0}\right\rceil  \tag{9}
\]
is a rational global Lipschitz constant for \(J(p,\cdot)\) on \([-G,G]\).  Equations (1)--(9) are finite rational receipts except for exponential inclusion in (6), whose finite receipt is supplied in Step 4 below; hence this construction is not circular in the interval oracle.

\emph{Step 2: exact one-dimensional point formula.}
Fix a rational \(g\in[-G,G]\).  Let \(w_g\) be the unnormalized density
\[
 w_g(x)=
 \begin{cases}
 e^{-Dx^2/(2q)},&x\leq g,\\
 e^{-dx^2/(2q)-\nu gx/q+\nu g^2/(2q)},&x>g.
 \end{cases}                                                     \tag{10}
\]
Set
\[
 s=-\frac{\nu g}{d},\qquad K=\frac{\nu Dg^2}{2qd},\qquad
 \sigma_D=\sqrt{q/D},\quad\sigma_d=\sqrt{q/d},                \tag{11}
\]
and write \(y_D(x)=x/\sigma_D\), \(y(x)=(x-s)/\sigma_d\), and \(y_g=y(g)\).  Completing the square on the right branch of (10) gives
\[
 w_g(x)=e^K\exp\{-(x-s)^2/(2\sigma_d^2)\},\qquad x>g.          \tag{12}
\]
Direct Gaussian integration now yields the exact normalizer and unnormalized first moment
\[
 \begin{aligned}
 Z={}&\sqrt{2\pi}\sigma_D\Phi(y_D(g))
 +e^K\sqrt{2\pi}\sigma_d\{1-\Phi(y_g)\},\\
 M={}&-\frac qD e^{-Dg^2/(2q)}
 +e^K\left[s\sqrt{2\pi}\sigma_d\{1-\Phi(y_g)\}
       +\frac qd e^{-y_g^2/2}\right].                           \tag{13}
 \end{aligned}
\]
Thus \(m_g=M/Z\).  For later use define
\[
 A_0(x)=\int_{-\infty}^xw_g(u)\,du,
 \qquad A_1(x)=\int_{-\infty}^xuw_g(u)\,du.                   \tag{14}
\]
For \(x\leq g\), elementary differentiation verifies
\[
 A_0(x)=\sqrt{2\pi}\sigma_D\Phi(y_D(x)),
 \qquad A_1(x)=-\frac qD e^{-Dx^2/(2q)}.                        \tag{15}
\]
For \(x>g\), continuity of the integrals at \(g\), (12), and the substitution \(v=(u-s)/\sigma_d\) give
\[
 \begin{aligned}
 A_0(x)={}&A_0(g)+e^K\sqrt{2\pi}\sigma_d
              \{\Phi(y(x))-\Phi(y_g)\},\\
 A_1(x)={}&A_1(g)+e^K\left[s\sqrt{2\pi}\sigma_d
              \{\Phi(y(x))-\Phi(y_g)\}
       +\frac qd\{e^{-y_g^2/2}-e^{-y(x)^2/2}\}\right].        \tag{16}
 \end{aligned}
\]
Let \(\Psi(x)=A_1(x)-m_gA_0(x)\).  By Definition \(\mathrm{diffusion\mbox{-}poisson}\),
\[
 h_g'(x)=-\frac{\Psi(x)}{q\,w_g(x)}.
\]
Since \(\pi_g=w_g/Z\), substitution into the definition of \(V_g\) proves the nonnested integral identity
\[
 V_g=\frac2{qZ}\int_{\mathbb R}\frac{\Psi(x)^2}{w_g(x)}\,dx. \tag{17}
\]
Thus every compact integrand needed for the point evaluator is an explicit composition of rational operations, square roots, exponentials, and \(\Phi\).

\emph{Step 3: certified tail truncation.}
The mode of \(w_g\) is
\[
 x^*=\begin{cases}0,&g\geq0,\\-\nu g/d,&g<0.\end{cases}       \tag{18}
\]
The potential has curvature between \(d/q\) and \(D/q\).  Integrating its derivative from its minimizer therefore gives, for every \(x\),
\[
 w_g(x^*)e^{-D(x-x^*)^2/(2q)}
 \leq w_g(x)
 \leq w_g(x^*)e^{-d(x-x^*)^2/(2q)}.                            \tag{19}
\]
After integrating the lower bound and dividing the upper bound by \(Z\),
\[
 \frac Z{w_g(x^*)}\geq\sqrt{\frac{2\pi q}{D}},
 \qquad
 \pi_g(x)\leq\sqrt{\frac D{2\pi q}}
 e^{-d(x-x^*)^2/(2q)}.                                        \tag{20}
\]
Choose an integer \(R>|g|+|x^*|\) and put \(r=R-|x^*|>0\).  The bound
\(\int_r^\infty e^{-du^2/(2q)}du\leq(q/(dr))e^{-dr^2/(2q)}\), obtained by replacing \(u/r\) by its lower bound one in the Gaussian derivative integral, and (20) imply
\[
 \mathbb P_{\pi_g}(|X|>R)
 \leq B_R:=\sqrt{\frac D{2\pi q}}\frac{2q}{dr}
 e^{-dr^2/(2q)}.                                                \tag{21}
\]
The Poisson-gradient bound in Theorem \(\mathrm{diffusion\mbox{-}poisson}\) consequently gives
\[
 0\leq2q\int_{|x|>R}\{h_g'(x)\}^2\pi_g(x)\,dx
 \leq\frac{2q}{d^2}B_R.                                       \tag{22}
\]
For a rational input box, use \(|x^*|\leq\nu_+|g|/d_-\) and outward-round the right sides of (21)--(22), replacing \(D,q,d\) monotonically by the bounds in (2)--(3) and using a rational lower enclosure of \(\pi\).  The resulting rational upper bound tends to zero as integer \(R\to\infty\), because its polynomial factor is dominated by \(\exp\{-d_-r^2/(2q_+)\}\).  Enumerating \(R\) therefore gives, after finitely many trials, any prescribed rational tail tolerance.

\emph{Step 4: finite rational elementary-function receipts.}
All transcendental enclosures used above have elementary finite rational certificates.  First,
\[
 \pi=16\arctan(1/5)-4\arctan(1/239),                            \tag{23}
\]
where (23) is verified by the rational tangent-addition formula and the fact that \(4\arctan(1/5)-\arctan(1/239)\in(0,\pi/2)\).  Integrating the finite geometric identity for \(1/(1+t^2)\) gives the alternating power series for \(\arctan x\) and its first-omitted-term remainder, hence nested rational enclosures of \(\pi\).  Positive square roots are enclosed by bisection, and every step is checked by squaring its rational endpoints.  For \(e^x\) at rational \(x\), choose an integer \(M>2|x|\), enclose \(e^{x/M}\) by its Taylor polynomial and the rational remainder bound
\[
 |R_n|\leq\frac{2|x/M|^{n+1}}{(n+1)!},                         \tag{24}
\]
which follows from \(e^{|x|/M}\leq\sum_{j\geq0}|x/M|^j\leq2\), and raise the resulting positive interval to the integer power \(M\).  Hence these exponential intervals shrink effectively to zero width.

For rational \(x\geq0\), integrate the exponential series to write
\[
 \Phi(x)=\frac12+\frac1{\sqrt{2\pi}}
 \sum_{j=0}^\infty\frac{(-1)^jx^{2j+1}}{2^j j!(2j+1)}.         \tag{25}
\]
After the terms begin decreasing, the alternating remainder is bounded by the first omitted term; symmetry handles negative \(x\).  Equations (23)--(25), together with rational interval operations, therefore give finite arbitrarily narrow enclosures of \(\Phi(x)\).

Finally, invert \(\Phi\) monotonically on \([0,H]\) to enclose \(z_\alpha\).  The input name supplies shrinking rational enclosures of \(1-\alpha/2\), and (25) supplies shrinking enclosures of every midpoint value.  If disjoint intervals decide the comparison, perform the corresponding bisection.  If they overlap, retain a symmetric bracket whose radius is the comparison uncertainty divided by a positive rational lower bound for
\[
 \phi(x)=(2\pi)^{-1/2}e^{-x^2/2},\qquad 0\leq x\leq H,         \tag{26}
\]
 obtained from (23)--(24).  Indeed, the difference of two values of \(\Phi\) is the integral of \(\phi\) between their arguments, so this positive lower bound makes the bracket valid.  Refining both input and function receipts makes its radius arbitrarily small, including when exact equality occurs at a tested midpoint.  Thus quantile inversion terminates at every requested width.  Each of (23)--(26) is certified by a finite list of rational terms, a rational remainder inequality, and outward-rounded rational arithmetic.

\emph{Step 5: terminating point evaluation.}
For a requested rational \(g\) and integer \(n\), dovetail four refinements: advance the input-name prefix; increase \(R\) until (22) is below the assigned error budget; lengthen the receipts in Step 4; and refine a rational partition of \([-R,g]\) and \([g,R]\).  On each cell, evaluate the appropriate formula (15) or (16) by outward rational interval arithmetic and enclose \(\Psi^2/w_g\) by its interval range.  The denominator is certified positive: (20) gives a positive lower bound for \(Z\), while (10) and the compactness of the current parameter box give a positive lower bound for \(w_g\) on \([-R,R]\).  The two expressions agree at \(g\), so there is no omitted kink contribution.

Multiplying each cell's rational range by its rational width gives lower and upper Darboux sums for the compact part of (17).  On each of the two closed branches the integrand is jointly continuous in \(x\) and in all parameters in a sufficiently refined positive input box.  Uniform continuity on that compact set implies that the maximum cell enclosure width tends to zero with the mesh and input widths.  The explicit tail bound (22) tends to zero with \(R\).  The elementary-function receipts tend to zero width by Step 4, and the lower denominator bounds keep division and the final square root uniformly continuous.  Therefore the dovetailing search terminates with a rational interval
\[
 P(g,n)=[P_-(g,n),P_+(g,n)]\ni J(p,g),
 \qquad P_+(g,n)-P_-(g,n)\leq2^{-n}.                            \tag{27}
\]
Here \(V_0=2\lambda\tau/d^3\) is evaluated directly, while \(V_g\) is evaluated by (13)--(17), \(z_\alpha\) by monotone inversion, and \(J\) by its defining formula.  A witness for (27) records the finite input prefix, \(R\), all series orders and remainder bounds, the partition, every cell range, both tail bounds, every bisection bracket, and every outward-rounded rational operation.  Hence (27) is a finite checkable evaluation witness, not an assumed real-number oracle.

\emph{Step 6: the interval oracle.}
For an admissible rational interval \(I=[a,b]\subseteq[-G,G]\), let \(g_0=(a+b)/2\), compute the point enclosure
\(P(g_0,m+1)=[P_-,P_+]\) from Step 5, and return
\[
 \mathfrak O(I,m)=
 \left[P_--\frac{L_J(b-a)}2,
       P_++\frac{L_J(b-a)}2\right].                            \tag{28}
\]
For every \(\eta\in I\), integrating the derivative bound (8)--(9) between \(g_0\) and \(\eta\) gives
\[
 |J(p,\eta)-J(p,g_0)|\leq L_J|\eta-g_0|
 \leq\frac{L_J(b-a)}2.                                        \tag{29}
\]
Combining (27)--(29) proves inclusion of \(J(p,\eta)\) in (28).  Its rational width obeys
\[
 \begin{aligned}
 \overline J(I,m)-\underline J(I,m)
 &=P_+-P_-+L_J(b-a)\\
 &\leq2^{-(m+1)}+L_J\operatorname{diam}(I)\\
 &\leq2^{-m}+L_J\operatorname{diam}(I).                        \tag{30}
 \end{aligned}
\]
If \(a=b\), (28) is just the point receipt and has width at most \(2^{-(m+1)}\leq2^{-m}\).  Thus (9) and (28), with the finite witnesses of Steps 1--5, satisfy every clause of Definition \(\mathrm{interval\mbox{-}oracle}\).  In particular, the moving kink is handled in a rational point evaluation split exactly at \(g_0\); no interval query relies on quadrature across an uncertain kink.  The already established oracle-conditional capacity-certificate theorem may now be applied to this constructed pair, but no part of the present construction assumes its soundness premise.

added_lemmas.statement:
For every \(p\in\mathcal P\) and \(\gamma\in[-G,G]\), write \(P_{\gamma,t}\) for the stationary semigroup generated by \(\mathcal L_\gamma\).  The potential \(-\log\pi_\gamma\), up to its normalizing constant, is continuously differentiable and piecewise quadratic, with second derivative at least \(d/q\) away from \(\gamma\).  If \(f\) is locally absolutely continuous and \(f,f'\in L^2(\pi_\gamma)\), then
\[
 \operatorname{Var}_{\pi_\gamma}(f)
 \leq \frac qd\int_{\mathbb R}\{f'(x)\}^2\pi_\gamma(x)\,dx .
\]
added_lemmas.proof_tex:
Fix \(p\in\mathcal P\) and \(\gamma\in[-G,G]\).  Put
\[
 b_\gamma(x)=-dx-\nu\min\{x,\gamma\}.
\]
The displayed density in the frozen core satisfies \(q(\log\pi_\gamma)'=b_\gamma\) on both sides of the kink.  The two one-sided derivatives agree at \(x=\gamma\), because each equals \(-D\gamma/q\).  Hence the potential \(U_\gamma=-\log\pi_\gamma\), with its additive normalizing constant suppressed, is continuously differentiable and
\[
 U_\gamma''(x)=
 \begin{cases}
 D/q,&x<\gamma,\\
 d/q,&x>\gamma.
 \end{cases}                                                     \tag{1}
\]
The rate assumptions give \(D=d+\nu>d>0\) and \(q>0\), so (1) proves the asserted curvature bound.

Let \(X_t^x\) and \(X_t^y\) solve the diffusion equation with drift \(b_\gamma\), diffusion coefficient \(\sqrt{2q}\), initial states \(x,y\), and the same Brownian path.  Since \(u\mapsto\min\{u,\gamma\}\) is nondecreasing,
\[
 (x-y)\{b_\gamma(x)-b_\gamma(y)\}
 \leq-d(x-y)^2.                                                  \tag{2}
\]
The Brownian terms cancel under this synchronous coupling.  Applying the ordinary chain rule away from the zero set of the difference and integrating the resulting differential inequality gives
\[
 |X_t^x-X_t^y|\leq e^{-dt}|x-y|.                                \tag{3}
\]
For smooth compactly supported \(f\), difference quotients in the initial state and (3) imply
\[
 |(P_{\gamma,t}f)'(x)|
 \leq e^{-dt}P_{\gamma,t}|f'|(x).                               \tag{4}
\]
Indeed, the stochastic flow derivative exists off the null set of paths hitting the single nondifferentiability point at the differentiation instant, is bounded by \(e^{-dt}\), and approximation of the Lipschitz drift by drifts with slopes in \([-D,-d]\) gives (4) without an exceptional initial state.  Jensen's inequality and invariance of \(\pi_\gamma\) therefore yield
\[
 \int\{(P_{\gamma,t}f)'\}^2\,d\pi_\gamma
 \leq e^{-2dt}\int P_{\gamma,t}(f'^2)\,d\pi_\gamma
 =e^{-2dt}\int f'^2\,d\pi_\gamma.                              \tag{5}
\]

The identity \(q(\log\pi_\gamma)'=b_\gamma\), integration by parts on the two half-lines, and continuity at the kink show that
\[
 -\int u\mathcal L_\gamma v\,d\pi_\gamma
 =q\int u'v'\,d\pi_\gamma                                    \tag{6}
\]
for smooth compactly supported \(u,v\); the boundary terms at \(\gamma\) cancel.  Apply (6) with \(u=v=P_{\gamma,t}f\).  Stationarity and the semigroup equation give
\[
 -\frac{d}{dt}\operatorname{Var}_{\pi_\gamma}(P_{\gamma,t}f)
 =2q\int\{(P_{\gamma,t}f)'\}^2\,d\pi_\gamma.                 \tag{7}
\]
For compactly supported Lipschitz \(f\), (3), coupled with an independent stationary initial state, shows that \(P_{\gamma,t}f\) converges in \(L^2(\pi_\gamma)\) to \(\int f\,d\pi_\gamma\); the Gaussian tails of the displayed invariant density make the coupling's second moment finite.  Integrating (7) from zero to infinity and then using (5) gives
\[
 \begin{aligned}
 \operatorname{Var}_{\pi_\gamma}(f)
 &=2q\int_0^\infty\int\{(P_{\gamma,t}f)'\}^2\,d\pi_\gamma\,dt\\
 &\leq2q\int_0^\infty e^{-2dt}\,dt
       \int(f')^2\,d\pi_\gamma
 =\frac qd\int(f')^2\,d\pi_\gamma.                            \tag{8}
 \end{aligned}
\]
Finally, truncate and mollify an arbitrary locally absolutely continuous \(f\) with \(f,f'\in L^2(\pi_\gamma)\).  Both sides of (8) converge by the \(L^2(\pi_\gamma)\) convergence of the functions and their derivatives.  This proves the stated inequality.

added_lemmas.statement:
For every \(p\in\mathcal P\), the map \(\gamma\mapsto V_\gamma(p)\) is continuously differentiable on the maintained staffing interval, with one-sided derivatives at its endpoints, and
\[
 \left|\frac{\partial V_\gamma(p)}{\partial\gamma}\right|
 \leq \frac{5\nu\sqrt q}{d^{5/2}}.
\]
Consequently, for all \(\gamma_1,\gamma_2\in[-G,G]\),
\[
 |V_{\gamma_1}(p)-V_{\gamma_2}(p)|
 \leq \frac{5\nu\sqrt q}{d^{5/2}}|\gamma_1-\gamma_2|.
\]
added_lemmas.proof_tex:
Fix \(p\in\mathcal P\).  It is convenient to use the unnormalized invariant density
\[
 w_\gamma(x)=
 \begin{cases}
 \exp\{-Dx^2/(2q)\},&x\leq\gamma,\\
 \exp\{-dx^2/(2q)-\nu\gamma x/q+\nu\gamma^2/(2q)\},&x>\gamma.
 \end{cases}                                                     \tag{1}
\]
The two branches and their first derivatives in \(x\) agree at \(x=\gamma\).  For fixed \(x\neq\gamma\),
\[
 r_\gamma(x):=\partial_\gamma\log w_\gamma(x)
 =-\frac\nu q(x-\gamma)_+,
 \qquad
 \dot b_\gamma(x):=\partial_\gamma b_\gamma(x)
 =-\nu\mathbf 1\{x>\gamma\}.                                  \tag{2}
\]
On every compact interval of values of \(\gamma\), (1)--(2) and their difference quotients are dominated by a polynomial times a Gaussian density.  Dominated convergence therefore gives
\[
 \partial_\gamma\pi_\gamma(x)
 =\pi_\gamma(x)\{r_\gamma(x)-\mathbb E_{\pi_\gamma}r_\gamma(X)\} \tag{3}
\]
in weighted \(L^1\), and permits differentiation of invariant expectations having a Gaussian-square-integrable envelope.

We next justify differentiation of the Poisson solution rather than assume it.  For \(u\neq0\), subtract the equations
\(-\mathcal L_{\gamma+u}h_{\gamma+u}=x-m_{\gamma+u}\) and
\(-\mathcal L_\gamma h_\gamma=x-m_\gamma\).  With
\(D_u h=(h_{\gamma+u}-h_\gamma)/u\) and
\(D_u b=(b_{\gamma+u}-b_\gamma)/u\), this gives the exact equation
\[
 -\mathcal L_\gamma D_u h
 =D_u b\,h_{\gamma+u}'-D_um.                                   \tag{4}
\]
Integration against \(\pi_\gamma\) shows that the right side of (4) is centered.  The monotonicity of the kink implies \(|D_ub|\leq\nu\), and Theorem \(\mathrm{diffusion\mbox{-}poisson}\) gives
\(0<h_{\gamma+u}'\leq1/d\) whenever \(u\) is sufficiently small.  Thus the variance of the right side of (4) is at most \(\nu^2/d^2\).  Multiplying (4) by its centered solution, using the integration-by-parts identity from Lemma \(\mathrm{stationary\mbox{-}poincare}\), Cauchy--Schwarz, and that lemma's Poincaré inequality gives
\[
 \begin{aligned}
 q\mathbb E_{\pi_\gamma}\{(D_uh')^2\}
 &\leq
 \sqrt{\operatorname{Var}_{\pi_\gamma}(D_uh)}\,
 \frac\nu d\\
 &\leq
 \sqrt{\frac qd\mathbb E_{\pi_\gamma}\{(D_uh')^2\}}\,
 \frac\nu d.
 \end{aligned}                                                   \tag{5}
\]
Consequently,
\[
 \mathbb E_{\pi_\gamma}\{(D_uh')^2\}
 \leq\frac{\nu^2}{qd^3}.                                      \tag{6}
\]
The explicit flux formula in Definition \(\mathrm{diffusion\mbox{-}poisson}\), (1), and dominated convergence give local convergence of \(h_{\gamma+u}'\) and of the right side of (4).  Bound (6) supplies uniform integrability in the Gaussian tails.  Hence every sequence \(u\to0\) has a weak stationary-Sobolev limit, and passing to (4) identifies that limit uniquely, by the Poincaré inequality, as \(k_\gamma=\partial_\gamma h_\gamma\), modulo the irrelevant additive constant.  Convergence is strong because the difference of two equations is bounded by the \(L^2\) difference of their right sides through the same calculation as (5).  We have proved
\[
 -\mathcal L_\gamma k_\gamma
 =\dot b_\gamma h_\gamma'-m_\gamma',
 \qquad
 m_\gamma'=\mathbb E_{\pi_\gamma}(\dot b_\gamma h_\gamma'),  \tag{7}
\]
where the second equality follows by integrating the first.  The same energy calculation yields
\[
 \mathbb E_{\pi_\gamma}\{(k_\gamma')^2\}
 \leq\frac{\nu^2}{qd^3}.                                      \tag{8}
\]

Since \(r_\gamma'(x)=-(\nu/q)\mathbf 1\{x>\gamma\}\) almost everywhere, Lemma \(\mathrm{stationary\mbox{-}poincare}\) also gives
\[
 \operatorname{Var}_{\pi_\gamma}(r_\gamma)
 \leq\frac qd\mathbb E_{\pi_\gamma}\{(r_\gamma')^2\}
 \leq\frac{\nu^2}{qd}.                                       \tag{9}
\]
Theorem \(\mathrm{diffusion\mbox{-}poisson}\) gives
\(1/D\leq h_\gamma'\leq1/d\).  Therefore
\(h_\gamma'^2\in[1/D^2,1/d^2]\), and the elementary estimate
\(\operatorname{Var}(Y)\leq(b-a)^2/4\) for \(Y\in[a,b]\) implies
\[
 \operatorname{Var}_{\pi_\gamma}(h_\gamma'^2)
 \leq\frac1{4d^4}.                                             \tag{10}
\]
Differentiating \(V_\gamma=2q\mathbb E_{\pi_\gamma}(h_\gamma'^2)\) by (3), (7), and the established Sobolev convergence gives
\[
 V_\gamma'
 =4q\mathbb E_{\pi_\gamma}(h_\gamma'k_\gamma')
  +2q\operatorname{Cov}_{\pi_\gamma}(h_\gamma'^2,r_\gamma). \tag{11}
\]
Using Cauchy--Schwarz, \(\mathbb E(h_\gamma'^2)\leq d^{-2}\), and (8)--(10), we obtain
\[
 \begin{aligned}
 |V_\gamma'|
 &\leq4q\left(\frac1{d^2}\frac{\nu^2}{qd^3}\right)^{1/2}
 +2q\left(\frac1{4d^4}\frac{\nu^2}{qd}\right)^{1/2}\\
 &=\frac{5\nu\sqrt q}{d^{5/2}}.                               \tag{12}
 \end{aligned}
\]
The domination following (2) and the strong Sobolev convergence above also make the derivative in (11) continuous.  Integrating (12) between any two points of the staffing interval proves the Lipschitz assertion; at \(-G\) and \(G\), the same argument gives the appropriate one-sided derivative.

proposed.statement:
From a supplied rational interval name \(\mathfrak r\) for \((p,c_M,c_I,\alpha,G)\), construct a positive rational \(L_J\) and, for every admissible rational interval \(I\subseteq[-G,G]\) and \(m\in\mathbb N\), rational endpoints \(\underline J(I,m)\) and \(\overline J(I,m)\), together with finite checkable evaluation witnesses derived from the piecewise-Gaussian Poisson-energy formulas for \(V_0\) and \(V_\gamma\), such that \((L_J,\mathfrak O)\) satisfies every enclosure, width, and point-width requirement of Definition \(\mathrm{interval\mbox{-}oracle}\) for \(J(p,\gamma)\).  In particular, the construction must certify the explicit uniform modulus
\[
 \overline J(I,m)-\underline J(I,m)
 \leq L_J\operatorname{diam}(I)+2^{-m}
\]
and must not take oracle soundness as an input premise.
proposed.justification: This theorem constructs the model-specific sound oracle and explicit rational modulus required for operational certification.
proposed.gap: The former oracle-construction gap is closed by finite rational transcendental receipts, explicit Gaussian tail bounds, split interval quadrature, and the proved energy Lipschitz modulus.
proposed.consumer: The constructed oracle supplies the premise of the conditional certificate theorem and thereby supports the finite-system regret guarantee.

proposed_core_edits.reason: The proof consumes the two directed analytic helpers, so the theorem's forward dependency metadata must expose them.

proposed.statement:
Conditional on a supplied sound interval oracle and the certificate returned by Theorem \(\mathrm{oracle\mbox{-}conditional\mbox{-}capacity\mbox{-}certificate}\), uniformly for \(p\in\mathcal P\), the certified offset satisfies
\[
 J_N(p,\gamma_\epsilon)-\inf_{|\gamma|\leq G}J_N(p,\gamma)
 \leq\epsilon+o(1).
\]
The conclusion is oracle-relative: it supplies no unconditional model-specific staffing recommendation while construction of the sound piecewise-Gaussian objective oracle remains open.

prose_updates.tldr: For equal-arm stationary homogeneous marked-history service experiments, the paper derives a compact-uniform joint occupation-and-rate-score Gaussian law from exact finite-chain Poisson martingales. Evaluating the exact stationary product law at the estimated rates while holding implemented capacity fixed yields fitted-center variance \(Q=A^{\mathsf T}\Gamma A\), residual variance \(W=V-Q\), and uniformly valid Wald coverage for arbitrary joint divergence of \(N\) and \(T_N\). The proved kink residual makes the diffusion center an \(O(N^{-1})\)-accurate corollary under \(T_N=o(N)\). For capacity choice, an explicit energy Lipschitz bound, Gaussian tail truncation, rational transcendental receipts, and split interval quadrature now construct the sound objective oracle; the existing branch-and-bound theorem then yields finite checkable capacity certificates.

project_justification.gap: The operational-dosage anchor permits distinct fixed arm populations and capacity and gives separate fixed-system occupation and many-system fluid results. It does not furnish the joint critical array law, marked-rate covariance, exact fixed-capacity plug-in inference, or certified critical-capacity optimization proved here for the narrower equal-arm stationary homogeneous subclass.
project_justification.niche: The finite-source birth--death product law makes the implemented finite-system effect exactly computable at candidate rates, while critical capacity creates a piecewise-diffusion score correction and a nontrivial kink. The same piecewise-Gaussian structure admits an explicit global energy modulus and a rational point evaluator whose quadrature is split exactly at the moving kink.
project_justification.fill: The paper proves stationary diffusion and Poisson-energy limits, a primitive martingale joint central limit law, the exact product-law fitted-center Wald theorem without a horizon upper bound, the uniform kink residual, and the diffusion corollary under \(T_N=o(N)\). It also constructs a sound model-specific rational objective oracle with finite receipts; combined with the generic branch-and-bound theorem and the uniform diffusion-energy transfer, this gives certified limiting-objective optimization and \(\epsilon+o(1)\) finite-system regret.

prose_updates.related_work: Boutilier, Jonasson, Li, and Yoeli allow distinct fixed arm populations and service capacity and establish separate fixed-system occupation and many-system fluid results. This paper studies the narrower equal-arm stationary compact homogeneous marked-history critical subclass and derives a joint population-duration limit there; it does not claim that positive results transfer upward to the broader anchor class. Braverman and Dai and Braverman inform the piecewise-diffusion and prelimit-Poisson residual methods. Hafouta informs uniform triangular-array reasoning, although the exact martingale proof here needs no upper horizon exponent. Wang and Plechac and Lok inform score--Poisson covariance and projection interpretations; the model-specific fixed-capacity derivative and exact product-law elbow are derived here. Borst, Mandelbaum, and Reiman motivate square-root staffing. The certification layer here is model-specific: it proves the energy modulus, normalizer and tail bounds, rational elementary-function enclosures, and split interval quadrature needed to instantiate the separately proved generic branch-and-bound semantics.
prose_updates.interpretation: The exact fitted interval targets the implemented stationary operational effect, not a diffusion estimand: at the true rates the product-law map equals \(\theta_N\) exactly. Same-path rate fitting projects the empirical occupation fluctuation onto the marked rate scores, producing fitted-center variance \(Q\) and empirical-minus-fitted variance \(W=V-Q\). The diffusion center is computationally simpler but inherits the additional \(T_N=o(N)\) condition from its proved \(O(N^{-1})\) approximation error. For design, the constructed rational oracle encloses the limiting capacity--precision objective with an explicit global modulus; applying the generic certificate theorem produces a checkable staffing offset, and the regret theorem transfers it to the finite system up to \(\epsilon+o(1)\).
prose_updates.technical_internal_limitation: The floating-point witness at \((\lambda,\tau,\nu,\gamma)=(1,1,1,0)\) remains diagnostic rather than a theorem output. The certification theorem is instead constructive at the level of finite rational receipts: it may refine the input name, truncation radius, series orders, quantile bracket, and Darboux partition without giving a practical worst-case running-time bound. The kink residual is proved uniformly, including kink-crossing jumps and ceiling phases, and \(K_{\mathrm{res}}\) is a proved finite constant. Marked recovery causes, stationary initialization, independent equal-sized arms, homogeneous compactly positive rates, and a bounded critical staffing window remain substantive restrictions.
prose_updates.honest_scope: Exact finite-chain fitted centering and empirical inference require only \(N,T_N\to\infty\); no upper relation between duration and enrollment is imposed. The diffusion fitted center differs by \(O_{\mathbb P}(N^{-1})\), so the proved route gives its Wald law under \(T_N/N\to0\). The paper does not claim results for the anchor's unequal-arm class, unmarked histories, common shocks, arbitrary initialization, heterogeneous rates, vanishing-rate boundaries, post-assignment randomization inference, or clinical cure effects. Capacity certification applies to the compact critical-offset objective encoded by a supplied rational interval name; it proves termination and finite checkability, not a uniform polynomial complexity bound.

statement_notes.gap: No oracle-soundness premise remains; the remaining limitation is computational efficiency, because termination is proved without a sharp worst-case complexity bound.
statement_notes.consumer: Together with the generic certificate theorem and the finite-design regret transfer, it yields a checkable staffing recommendation for the stated compact model class.
